title: Strict ref validation for planner write commands
summary: Make all planner write tools resolve human refs or fail explicitly; never persist broken parent links.
description: Urgent reliability phase prompted by a real planner integrity bug discovered while creating P034/F005 work. In the current Pi adapter implementation, some write tools describe parameters as human refs (`F00x`, `P00x`, `T00x`, shortId, title) but internally treat fields like `featureId` as already-resolved internal IDs. In particular, `phase_create` in `packages/pi-adapter/src/index.ts:3063-3118` and `phase_update` in `packages/pi-adapter/src/index.ts:3122-3202` can accept a string that looks like `F005`, persist it into `phase.featureId`, and continue instead of rejecting the unresolved parent. That allowed creation of a phase orphaned from its feature until manually relinked. The same risk area must be audited across planner write commands in both adapters: Pi tool registrations in `packages/pi-adapter/src/index.ts:2856-3612` and MCP handlers in `packages/plan-mcp/src/index.ts:390-925`, especially create/update/delete/start/complete flows that receive feature/phase/task references or parent ids. Existing resolver helpers already exist (`findFeatureByRef` in `packages/pi-adapter/src/index.ts:1197`, shared `findPhaseByRef` / `findTaskByRef`, and the MCP-local `findFeatureByRef` in `packages/plan-mcp/src/index.ts:70`), but they are applied inconsistently. Goal: every planner write command must either resolve the incoming human ref to a real entity before any mutation or return a clear validation error; no command may silently persist an unresolved parent link or ambiguous reference. Behaviors to preserve: human-friendly refs remain accepted, globally unique `P00x/T00x` support remains intact, and tool error messages stay explicit and actionable.

tasks.title: Enforce resolved feature refs in pi-adapter write tools
tasks.description:
Fix the Pi adapter write-tool paths so any incoming feature reference is resolved or rejected before persistence. Current risk area: `feature_create`/`feature_update` are fine because they act on features directly, but `phase_create` (`packages/pi-adapter/src/index.ts:3063-3118`) and `phase_update` (`packages/pi-adapter/src/index.ts:3122-3202`) currently accept a `featureId` parameter described to users as a feature ref while the implementation writes `params.featureId` directly into `phase.featureId` and only conditionally updates the feature document if an internal-id match exists. This must be changed so `F005`, shortId, UUID, and title-like feature refs are resolved through a shared helper before mutation; unresolved or ambiguous refs must return a clear error and abort the write. Audit adjacent write commands in `packages/pi-adapter/src/index.ts:2856-3612` for the same pattern anywhere a parent ref or entity ref is accepted. Preserve existing support for human refs and explicit UUIDs, but make validation strict and fail-closed.

---
**Completion summary:**
Hardened feature-ref validation in the Pi adapter write tools.

Changes in `packages/pi-adapter/src/index.ts`:
- Added top-level strict resolver `resolveFeatureRefStrict(features, ref)` near the shared helper block (after `taskLabel`).
- The resolver now accepts human refs (`F00x`, shortId, UUID, exact/unique name, unique partial name) and returns explicit validation errors for empty, unresolved, or ambiguous refs.
- Applied the strict resolver to write paths that accept feature refs:
  - `feature_update`
  - `feature_delete`
  - `phase_create` (parent feature resolution before lock/save/priority assignment)
  - `phase_update` (re-linking `featureId` now resolves or errors; unlink via empty string still supported)
- `phase_create` no longer persists raw unresolved strings into `phase.featureId` and no longer links against a non-existent parent silently.

Behaviors preserved:
- human-friendly refs remain accepted
- UUID/internal ids remain accepted
- explicit unlink with `featureId: ""` in `phase_update` still works

Validation:
- `pnpm --filter @agent-plan/pi-adapter build`
- `pnpm check`

Remaining follow-up tracked separately:
- MCP parity in `T139(P035/F005)`
- cross-adapter regression coverage in `T140(P035/F005)`.

tasks.title: Align plan-mcp write handlers with strict ref validation
tasks.description:
Audit and fix the MCP write handlers so they match the same strict reference-resolution rules as the Pi adapter. Relevant code paths are in `packages/plan-mcp/src/index.ts:390-925`, where the MCP layer uses a local `findFeatureByRef` (`packages/plan-mcp/src/index.ts:70`) and shared `findPhaseByRef` / `findTaskByRef` in multiple handlers. Any command that accepts a feature/phase/task ref or parent ref must resolve it before mutating planner data, and must return a clear validation error if the ref is invalid, unresolved, or ambiguous. This includes create/update/delete/start/complete flows, especially parent-linking operations analogous to the broken Pi `phase_create/phase_update` path. Preserve the public command surface and human-friendly refs, but ensure the MCP harness cannot create or update planner entities with broken parent links or silent no-op relationships.

---
**Completion summary:**
Aligned MCP feature-ref handling with the same strict validation model used for the Pi adapter.

Changes in `packages/plan-mcp/src/index.ts`:
- Hardened `findFeatureByRef(features, ref)` so read/filter flows now understand:
  - `F00x`
  - shortId
  - UUID/internal id
  - exact name
  - partial name fallback
- Added `resolveFeatureRefStrict(features, ref)` returning explicit outcomes for:
  - empty ref
  - unresolved ref
  - ambiguous exact-name matches
  - ambiguous partial-name matches
- Applied strict resolution to MCP handlers that mutate planner state or link parents:
  - `planner-feature-update`
  - `planner-feature-delete`
  - `planner-phase-add` (resolves optional parent feature before lock/save/link)
- Also applied strict resolution to `planner-feature-show` so direct single-entity lookup no longer silently picks an arbitrary partial/ambiguous feature.

Integrity effect:
- MCP can no longer create/update/delete against an ambiguous or unresolved feature ref.
- `planner-phase-add` can no longer persist a broken `phase.featureId` parent link from a human ref string.

Validation:
- `pnpm --filter @agent-plan/mcp build`
- `pnpm check`

Remaining follow-up:
- `T140(P035/F005)` for cross-adapter validation coverage of invalid and human refs.

tasks.title: Add cross-adapter validation tests for invalid and human refs
tasks.description:
Add regression coverage for strict planner reference validation so this class of corruption cannot reappear silently. Cover both adapters and shared behaviors: valid human refs (`F00x`, `P00x`, `T00x`, shortId, title where unambiguous), explicit UUIDs/internal ids, unresolved refs, and ambiguous refs. Include negative cases proving that commands abort with a readable validation error and do not persist changes when a parent feature/phase/task cannot be resolved. Focus on the currently risky write surfaces identified in `packages/pi-adapter/src/index.ts:3063-3612` and `packages/plan-mcp/src/index.ts:390-925`, and reuse shared resolver behavior where possible. Also validate that globally unique phase/task short refs still work after the stricter checks. Deliverable: tests plus a brief audit note on which commands were hardened.

---
**Completion summary:**
Added cross-adapter regression coverage for strict planner ref validation.

New tests:
- `packages/pi-adapter/test/ref-validation.test.mjs`
- `packages/plan-mcp/test/ref-validation.test.mjs`

Coverage added:
- Pi adapter
  - `phase_create` resolves valid human feature refs (`F001`) to internal feature ids
  - `phase_create` rejects unresolved feature refs (`F999`) without persisting a phase
  - `phase_update` rejects unresolved relink refs and preserves the current parent feature
  - `feature_update` rejects ambiguous partial refs (`Auth`) without mutating data
  - `task_get` still resolves globally unique `T001` refs after the stricter feature validation changes
- MCP adapter
  - `planner-phase-add` resolves valid human feature refs (`F001`) to internal feature ids
  - `planner-phase-add` rejects unresolved feature refs (`F999`) without persisting a phase
  - `planner-feature-update` rejects ambiguous partial refs (`Auth`) without mutating data
  - `planner-feature-delete` rejects ambiguous partial refs (`Auth`) without deleting data
  - `planner-task-show` still resolves globally unique `T001` refs after the stricter feature validation changes

Audit note on hardened commands:
- Pi adapter write paths hardened in T138:
  - `feature_update`
  - `feature_delete`
  - `phase_create`
  - `phase_update`
- MCP write paths hardened in T139:
  - `planner-feature-update`
  - `planner-feature-delete`
  - `planner-phase-add`
- Read-path regression check retained for global task refs:
  - Pi `task_get`
  - MCP `planner-task-show`

Validation run:
- `node --test packages/pi-adapter/test/ref-validation.test.mjs packages/plan-mcp/test/ref-validation.test.mjs`
- `pnpm check`
- `git diff --check`
